title: I Think We're Forgetting How to Be Bored
why_read: A reflective personal essay about losing the capacity for boredom in a hyperconnected world, with no technical content relevant to software engineering.
analysis: This is a lifestyle/wellbeing essay musing on how smartphones have eliminated unstructured 'boredom' time and what might be lost as a result, framed around a personal anecdote about reaching for a phone during idle moments. It contains no code, system design, or technical argument and is purely reflective writing about attention and modern habits. It may resonate emotionally with some readers but offers nothing of technical substance for a software engineering digest.
